anc_visits.title: First ANC Visit (Before 12 weeks)
anc_visits.description: First antenatal care visit should be conducted before 12 weeks of pregnancy to establish baseline health status and identify risk factors.
key_points: Complete medical history and physical examination
Urine examination for protein and sugar
guidelines: Should be conducted at a health facility
Should provide iron and folic acid supplementation
Must counsel on diet and rest
warnings: High blood pressure requires immediate referral
HIV positive cases need special care

anc_visits.title: Second ANC Visit (16-24 weeks)
anc_visits.description: Second visit focuses on monitoring pregnancy progress and identifying any complications.
guidelines: Must check for signs of pre-eclampsia
warnings: Excessive weight gain may indicate problems
High blood pressure needs immediate attention

complications.title: Hypertension in Pregnancy
complications.description: High blood pressure during pregnancy can lead to serious complications for both mother and baby. potentially leading to preterm birth. Regular prenatal care visits and home blood pressure monitoring are crucial.
management: Immediate referral to higher facility
Monitor blood pressure closely
Bed rest in left lateral position
Antihypertensive medication if needed
Pharmacological management with safe antihypertensive drugs (Labetalol, Nifedipine controlled release)
Maintain blood pressure within 110–140/80–90 mmHg
Low-dose aspirin (150 mg daily) for high-risk for preeclampsia (12–16 weeks until 36 weeks)
Urgent management for severe hypertension (≥160/110 mmHg) with IV Hydralazine, Labetalol, or oral Nifedipine
procedures: Measure blood pressure in sitting position
Initiate low-dose aspirin for high-risk cases
Manage severe cases at specialist centers with inpatient care and protocols
warnings: Severe hypertension is a medical emergency
Avoid ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics, most other beta-blockers and calcium channel antagonists due to fetal effects
Severe cases require management at specialist centers

safe_drugs.dose: 100 mg twice a day to 400 mg three times a day
30 mg daily to 60 mg twice a day

contraindicated_drugs: Most other beta-blockers and calcium channel antagonists

general_care.title: General Pregnancy Care Guidelines
general_care.description: Essential care guidelines for all pregnant women to ensure healthy pregnancy and delivery.
guidelines: Should have at least 4 ANC visits
Must take iron and folic acid tablets
procedures: Provide iron and folic acid tablets

abortion_care.title: Comprehensive Abortion Care (CAC) and the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021
abortion_care.description: CAC is a vital component of the RMNCH+A strategy. The Medical Termination of Pregnancy (Amendment) Act, 2021, expands access to safe, affordable, and legal abortion services.
key_provisions: Opinion from one registered medical practitioner for termination up to 20 weeks.
Opinion from two registered medical practitioners for termination between 20 and 24 weeks.
Upper gestation limit extended to 24 weeks for vulnerable groups.
No gestation limits for substantial fetal abnormalities diagnosed by a Medical Board.
Extension of contraceptive failure clause to include both woman and partner.
warnings: Unsafe abortions attributed to 8% of maternal deaths (2001-03).

procedures.title: Normal Delivery Procedure
procedures.description: Step-by-step procedure for conducting a normal delivery safely.
guidelines: Should be conducted in a clean environment
Should provide emotional support to mother

emergency_procedures.title: Emergency Delivery Procedures
emergency_procedures.description: Procedures to follow in emergency situations during delivery, including management of Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH) and Eclampsia.
key_points: Stay calm and reassure the mother
guidelines: Should have emergency contact numbers ready

emergencies_covered.title: Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH)
emergencies_covered.definition: Blood loss ≥ 500 ml within 24 hours after birth (severe PPH ≥ 1000 ml)
key_points: Leading cause of maternal death worldwide
prevention_management: Active management of third stage of labor (uterotonic, delayed cord clamping, controlled cord traction, uterine massage)
Maintain hemorrhage cart with essential supplies
Implement emergency release and massive transfusion protocols
Quantitative measurement of cumulative blood loss
Patient education on PPH risk and early warning signs

community_based_misoprostol_distribution.description: ASHAs and ANMs permitted to undertake advance distribution of Misoprostol tablets for PPH prevention in remote areas.
community_based_misoprostol_distribution.dosage: Three 200 mcg tablets (total 600 mcg) orally, self-administered just after delivery
conditionalities: Rule out multiple pregnancy or other contraindications (previous Cesarean section, multiple pregnancy, severe PIH/anemia, cardiac disease)

emergencies_covered.title: Eclampsia
emergencies_covered.description: Severe complication of pregnancy characterized by seizures.
management: Magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) is preferred anticonvulsant
Antihypertensive drugs (Labetalol, Hydralazine, Nifedipine) to control blood pressure
Definitive treatment is delivery of the baby
Acute care during a seizure is critical and involves immediate medical interventions to manage the airway, breathing, and circulation, while also ensuring patient safety during convulsions
Administer oxygen, lateral decubitus position, suction oral secretions, cardiac monitoring, IV line, careful fluid management to avoid overload or hypoperfusion

issues: MgSO4 recognized as the 'gold standard' but inconsistent availability/utilization
Policy ambiguities (classified as 'level-T' drug but permitted at PHCs/CHCs)
Poor inventory management leading to stock-outs

iphs_labor_rooms.title: Indian Public Health Standards (IPHS) for Labor Rooms
iphs_labor_rooms.description: Detailed guidelines for the planning, infrastructure, and operational protocols of labor rooms at Primary Health Centres (PHCs) and Urban Primary Health Centres (UPHCs).

details: Specifications for number of labor tables/beds based on delivery load
Features for labor beds (e.g., adjustable side rails, Trendelenburg/reverse positions, hydraulic height adjustment)
Room components: nursing stations, newborn care areas, toilets, handwashing areas
Radiant warmers, hand-held fetal dopplers, autoclaved delivery trays, resuscitation kits, glucometers
Biomedical waste (BMW) management protocols (segregation, disinfection, storage, disposal in color-coded bins)
Adequate quantities of essential consumables such as cotton, gauze, IV drip sets, needles, oral and parenteral medicines
Disposable mother and baby supplies (e.g., baby receiving sheets, caps, socks, cord clamps)
Specific staffing norms are provided for ANMs, staff nurses, medical officers (including OBG/EmOC specialists, anesthetists/LSAS, and pediatricians), and support staff
Recommendations for non-rotation of labor room personnel to maintain expertise and continuity of care

details.triaging: Categorizing clients into normal delivery (nurse-led) and those needing obstetrician care (specialist-led)
details.disinfection_sterilization: Procedures for instruments and linen, including immediate soaking in chlorine solution, cleaning, autoclaving, and proper storage
details.cleaning_labor_room: Daily and post-delivery cleaning with disinfectants, specific mopping procedures, and maintenance of a dry environment
details.entry_protocols: Requiring a buffer zone for changing shoes, wearing masks and caps, and restricting entry to essential personnel to maintain a sterile environment
safe_care_dos: Active management of the third stage of labor (AMTSL)
Essential newborn care (drying and wrapping, immediate resuscitation if needed, skin-to-skin contact, early initiation of breastfeeding, Injection Vitamin K)
Assessment of maternal bleeding and newborn condition
Use of the Safe Childbirth Checklist (SCC) at various checkpoints
harmful_practices_donts: Routine induction/augmentation of labor (unless C-section capable)

care_guidelines.title: Immediate Postpartum Care
care_guidelines.description: Care provided immediately after delivery to ensure mother and baby are safe. Guidelines emphasize daily monitoring of the newborn and mother, comprehensive post-discharge counseling, and ensuring a minimum of six postnatal home visits by ASHAs up to 42 days after birth, with at least one supervised visit by an ANM.
guidelines: Ensure a minimum of six postnatal home visits by ASHAs up to 42 days after birth.
At least one supervised postnatal visit by an ANM.

care_guidelines.title: Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) for Low Birth Weight (LBW) Babies
care_guidelines.description: Evidence-based intervention improving health and well-being of LBW babies through thermal control, breastfeeding promotion, infection prevention, and bonding.
components: Skin-to-skin contact: early, continuous, prolonged contact between mother/caregiver and baby on chest.
Exclusive breastfeeding: babies receiving KMC are exclusively breastfed.
prerequisites: Support to the mother in hospital and at home (counseling, supervision, family assistance)
Post-discharge follow-up: regular follow-up and accessible health providers for home-based KMC.
care_guidelines.suitability: All stable LBW babies (typically >1800g initially), with specific guidelines for positioning and monitoring.
implementation_challenges: Socio-cultural barriers (skin-to-skin culturally inappropriate, lack of personal space, misconceptions about roles, burden on mother)
Misconceptions among healthcare professionals (less enthusiastic promotion)
Perceived burden on staff (obtaining consent, teaching methods, assisting feeding, follow-up)
Lack of clear policies and adequate infrastructure (lack of specific policies, space, reclining chairs)

care_guidelines.title: Essential Newborn Care
care_guidelines.description: Basic care procedures for newborns to ensure their health and survival.

programs.title: Navjaat Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (NSSK)
programs.description: Launched in 2009, NSSK aims to equip doctors and nurses with the knowledge and skills required to provide essential newborn care around birth, aligning with India Newborn Action Plan (2014) and National Health Policy-2017's goal of achieving single-digit Neonatal Mortality Rate (NMR) by 2030.
key_points: Capacity building for healthcare providers in essential newborn care
Aims to reduce NMR to single digit by 2030

traditional_practices.title: Traditional Newborn Care Practices and Beliefs
traditional_practices.description: Traditional newborn care practices and beliefs persist in many communities, with both beneficial and harmful implications.

harmful_practices.details: 61.1% receive prelacteal feeds (sugar water, honey, butter) for 1-3 days. Only 38.9% receive colostrum. Beliefs: 'stagnant impure milk', 'not good for health', 'cannot be digested', 'forms hard stool', 'pure milk not secreted'. Can predispose to infections.
94.9% apply substances (sweet flag, coconut oil, turmeric powder) to cord stump to prevent early drying/air entry into stomach. Unsterile blades/knives used in some home deliveries.
71.2% bathed before cord drops off (23.7% within 24h, 47.5% on 2nd day).
Blowing into nostrils (45.7%). Beliefs about evil spirits: not leaving house in first month, applying kajal (16.9%), or not drying newborns' clothes outside the house.

Traditional healers are often approached for skin infections (42.4%), and herbal medications are used for diarrhea (40.6%) and cold (25.4%). For colic, sweet flag application (8.5%) and castor oil massage are common.

traditional_practices.implications: Highlights gap in health education and behavior change communication. Requires culturally sensitive approaches.

vaccines.title: Tetanus Toxoid for Pregnant Women
vaccines.description: Tetanus toxoid vaccination to protect mother and newborn from tetanus.
vaccines.name: TT
key_points: First dose at first ANC visit
guidelines: Should be given to all pregnant women
Must be given at least 2 weeks before delivery

digital_platform.title: U-WIN (Digital Vaccination Platform)
digital_platform.description: Launched in October 2024 for complete digitization of vaccination services and maintaining comprehensive vaccination records for pregnant women and children from birth up to 17 years under the Universal Immunization Programme.
key_points: Comprehensive vaccination records for pregnant women and children (0-17 years)
Aims to improve data accuracy, streamline record-keeping, and enhance program efficiency

guidelines.title: Pregnancy Nutrition Guidelines
guidelines.description: Evidence‑based dietary requirements for pregnant women in India.
key_points: ≥65 g protein/day (dal, eggs, milk, lean meat)
Daily IFA 100 mg iron + 0.5 mg folic acid × 100 days (National Iron + Initiative)
1 tablet calcium (500 mg) twice daily away from IFA
Adequate fluids ≥2.5 L, emphasize safe water
guidelines: Include at least 5 servings of fruit/vegetables
Weekly fish/omega‑3 rich food unless contra‑indicated
Daily milk/curd for calcium & vitamin D
Limit caffeine <200 mg/day; avoid alcohol & tobacco

taboos_and_misconceptions.myth: Papaya or pineapple always cause miscarriage
taboos_and_misconceptions.evidence: Ripe fruit is safe; only unripe/raw papaya latex has uterotonic effect.
taboos_and_misconceptions.action: Allow ripe papaya/pineapple in moderation for vitamins A & C.

taboos_and_misconceptions.myth: Eggs and meat make the baby 'big' and delivery difficult
taboos_and_misconceptions.action: Encourage 1 egg/day if affordable; monitor weight gain.

taboos_and_misconceptions.myth: Pregnant women should avoid milk when they have cough/cold
taboos_and_misconceptions.evidence: No scientific basis; calcium need rises in pregnancy.

procedures: Counsel with local food examples & portion sizes
Monthly weight check, MUAC if under‑weight
Link to take‑home rations / THR under ICDS where available
warnings: Avoid raw or under‑cooked meat, fish & eggs (listeriosis risk)
Restrict processed foods high in salt & trans‑fat
No herbal/home remedies without medical advice

national_initiatives.title: Mission Poshan 2.0
national_initiatives.description: Flagship program addressing malnutrition, aiming to improve health, wellness, and immunity through community engagement, outreach, behavioral change, and advocacy. Focuses on maternal nutrition, infant/young child feeding, SAM/MAM treatment, and wellness promotion via AYUSH practices.
key_points: Reduce wasting, underweight prevalence, stunting, and anemia
Supply of fortified rice (iron, folic acid, Vitamin B12) under TPDS, PM-POSHAN, ICDS

emergencies.title: Severe Bleeding During Pregnancy
emergencies.description: Emergency management of severe bleeding during pregnancy. also known as Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH) if occurring after birth. PPH is defined as blood loss ≥ 500 ml within 24 hours after birth (severe PPH ≥ 1000 ml) and is the leading cause of maternal death worldwide.
management: Immediate referral to hospital
Keep woman lying down
Elevate legs if possible
Monitor vital signs
Arrange transportation
Active management of the third stage of labor (uterotonic, delayed cord clamping, controlled cord traction, uterine massage) is strongly recommended for prevention.
Health facilities should maintain a hemorrhage cart, rapid response team, and implement emergency release and massive transfusion protocols.
Community-based Misoprostol distribution by ASHAs/ANMs in remote areas (3x200 mcg tablets orally after delivery, with counseling and contraindication checks).
procedures: Quantitative measurement of cumulative blood loss.
warnings: Contraindications for Misoprostol distribution: previous Cesarean section, multiple pregnancy, severe PIH/anemia, cardiac disease.

emergencies.title: Eclampsia
emergencies.description: Severe complication of pregnancy characterized by seizures, requiring immediate and expert management.
management: Magnesium sulfate (MgSO4) is the preferred anticonvulsant.
Antihypertensive drugs (Labetalol, Hydralazine, Nifedipine) to control blood pressure.
Definitive treatment is delivery of the baby.

Acute care during seizure: manage airway, breathing, circulation, ensure patient safety (administer oxygen, lateral decubitus position, suction oral secretions, cardiac monitoring, IV line, careful fluid management).
warnings: Policy ambiguities regarding MgSO4 classification ('level-T' drug vs. use at PHCs/CHCs) and poor inventory management can lead to stock-outs.
Requires immediate hospitalization and specialist care.

issues: MgSO4 recognized as 'gold standard' but inconsistent availability/utilization
Policy ambiguities (classified as 'level-T' drug but permitted by trained nurses/midwives at PHCs/CHCs)
Poor inventory management leading to stock-outs

guidelines.title: ASHA Worker Responsibilities
guidelines.description: General responsibilities and guidelines for ASHA workers in maternal care.
key_points: Create awareness and provide information on health determinants (nutrition, sanitation, hygiene)
Counsel women on birth preparedness, safe delivery, breastfeeding, immunization, contraception, infection prevention
Mobilize community and facilitate access to health services (immunization, ANC, PNC, ICDS)
Arrange escorts/accompany pregnant women/children to health facilities
Provide primary medical care for minor ailments and first aid
Serve as depot holders for essential provisions (ORS, IFA, chloroquine, DDKs, OCPs, condoms)
Inform sub-centers/PHCs about births, deaths, unusual health problems/disease outbreaks
Collaborate with Village Health & Sanitation Committee for village health plans
guidelines: Selection criteria: women residents of village, preferably married, widowed, or divorced, and generally in the age group of 25 to 45 years. They should possess effective communication skills, leadership qualities, and be able to reach out to the community. A minimum formal education up to the Eighth Class is required, though this criterion may be relaxed if no suitable candidate with this qualification is available.
warnings: Do not perform procedures beyond training

programs_involved.title: Home-Based Newborn Care (HBNC)
programs_involved.description: ASHAs conduct six or seven home visits for newborns during the critical first 42 days after birth. For home deliveries, an additional visit is made on the day of birth.
programs_involved.visits: 6-7 home visits in first 42 days (additional for home deliveries)

programs_involved.title: Home-Based Care for Young Child (HBYC)
programs_involved.description: ASHAs undertake five additional home visits for children at the completion of 3, 6, 9, 12, and 15 months of age.
objectives: Improve nutritional status of young children
Ensure proper growth and early childhood development

programs_involved.title: Community-Based Misoprostol Distribution
programs_involved.description: ASHAs play a vital role in distributing Misoprostol for PPH prevention in areas where institutional delivery is unlikely. They provide 3x200 mcg tablets orally to pregnant women in their 8th month for self-administration after delivery, with training and conditionalities.

incentivization_and_support: Incentivized for various tasks (e.g., tracking high-risk pregnancies under e-PMSMA, distributing Misoprostol for PPH prevention).
Incentives linked to healthy outcomes, meeting conditionalities and reporting requirements.

maternal_schemes.title: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)
maternal_schemes.description: Launched in 2011 to eliminate out-of-pocket expenses for institutional delivery and neonatal care. Covers all pregnant women delivering in public health institutions and sick newborns.
maternal_schemes.eligibility: All pregnant women delivering in public health institutions
benefits: Free diet (3 days normal, 7 days C-section)
Free transport (home to facility, inter-facility, drop-back)
Covers all antenatal and postnatal pregnancy complications
how_to_apply: Present MCP card and ID proof
key_points: Available at all public health institutions
guidelines: Must inform pregnant women about JSSK benefits
procedures: Help pregnant woman register at facility
warnings: Only available at public health institutions

maternal_schemes.title: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA)
maternal_schemes.description: Free quality ANC (check‑ups, USG, lab tests) for all pregnant women on the 9th of every month at government facilities. Includes Extended PMSMA (e-PMSMA) launched in January 2022 to ensure quality ANC for women with high-risk pregnancies (HRP) and facilitates individual tracking of these HRP cases until a safe delivery is achieved. Financial incentivization is provided to identified HRP women and ASHAs for extra follow-up visits.
benefits: One assured ANC by specialist/MBBS doctor
how_to_apply: Visit designated PMSMA clinic on the 9th of any month
key_points: Free quality ANC on 9th of every month
Financial incentives for HRP women and ASHAs for follow-up
guidelines: Must inform pregnant women about PMSMA
Must identify and track high-risk pregnancies
procedures: Facilitate individual tracking of HRP cases
Provide financial incentives to HRP women and ASHAs for follow-up
warnings: Only available on 9th of each month
Ensure proper identification and management of HRP cases

high_risk_pregnancy_categories.category: H/O Still Birth (History of Still Birth)

maternal_schemes.title: Anemia‑Mukt Bharat / Intensified National Iron Plus Initiative (I‑NIPI)
maternal_schemes.description: Six‑point strategy to reduce anemia among women, children & adolescents through prophylactic IFA, deworming, and social behavior change. Employs a comprehensive '6x6x6 strategy' encompassing six beneficiary age groups, six interventions, and six institutional mechanisms.
benefits: Daily IFA 60 mg elemental iron + 0.5 mg folic acid
Use of sugar-coated IFA tablets for adherence
Digital methods for routine testing and treatment
Fortified rice and double fortified salt
IV iron formulations (FCM) for rapid iron replenishment
how_to_apply: IFA distributed during ANC or ASHA home visit
Hemoglobin test at sub‑centre or PHC
key_points: Intensified Year-Round Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) Campaigns
Routine Testing and Treatment for Anemia (digital methods, point-of-care)
Mandatory Provision of Fortified Foods (fortified rice, double fortified salt)
Use of Intravenous (IV) Iron Sucrose/Ferric Carboxymaltose (FCM) for moderate to severe anemia
guidelines: Should promote delayed cord clamping in newborns
Must ensure consistent availability of essential drugs
Should address policy ambiguities and supply chain issues
procedures: Administer IV iron formulations as per protocol
warnings: IFA should be taken on empty stomach
Address policy ambiguities for drug classification (e.g., MgSO4)
Improve inventory management to prevent stock-outs

maternal_schemes.title: Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) Initiative
maternal_schemes.description: Promotes continuous skin‑to‑skin contact & exclusive breastfeeding for LBW/ preterm newborns ≤2000 g.
how_to_apply: Initiate KMC in facility once newborn stable
Continue at home with ASHA support
guidelines: Should initiate KMC immediately after birth

maternal_schemes.title: Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan (SUMAN)
maternal_schemes.description: Launched in 2019, SUMAN is a significant initiative aimed at providing assured, dignified, respectful, and quality healthcare to every woman and newborn visiting public health facilities. The program operates with a zero-tolerance policy for denial of services, striving to eliminate all preventable maternal and newborn deaths.
maternal_schemes.eligibility: Every woman and newborn visiting public health facilities
benefits: Assured, dignified, respectful, and quality healthcare
Zero-tolerance policy for denial of services
Elimination of preventable maternal and newborn deaths
how_to_apply: Access services at public health facilities
key_points: Aims to eliminate preventable maternal and newborn deaths

maternal_schemes.title: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY)
maternal_schemes.description: Maternity benefit program providing financial assistance of Rs. 5000/- to women for their first living child, subject to the fulfillment of certain conditionalities. This scheme aims to provide partial wage compensation for wage loss during pregnancy and childbirth and to provide conditions for safe delivery and good nutrition and feeding practices.
maternal_schemes.eligibility: Women for their first living child
benefits: Partial wage compensation for wage loss
Support for safe delivery and good nutrition/feeding practices
key_points: Financial assistance for first living child
Aims to reduce wage loss and promote healthy practices

child_schemes.title: Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK)
child_schemes.description: Targets children birth to 18 years. Detects and intervenes early for 4Ds: defects at birth, deficiencies, diseases, developmental delays/disabilities.
benefits: Reduces disease burden and family expenses
key_points: Covers 4Ds: Defects, Deficiencies, Diseases, Developmental delays
guidelines: Must refer detected cases to specialists
Should follow up on treatment compliance

adolescent_schemes.title: Rashtriya Kishor Swasthya Karyakram (RKSK)
adolescent_schemes.description: Targets adolescents (10–19 years), married and unmarried. Focus on reproductive and sexual health, nutrition, mental health, substance misuse, gender-based violence, NCDs.
key_points: Delays marriage and reduces teen pregnancy

immunization_schemes.title: Universal Immunization Programme (UIP)
immunization_schemes.description: Provides free vaccination against 13 life-threatening diseases for newborns and pregnant women across the country, with costs entirely borne by the central government.
how_to_apply: Attend immunization session at nearest health centre
guidelines: Must ensure all children are vaccinated
Must follow up on missed vaccinations
warnings: Vaccination schedule must be followed strictly

nationally_covered: Meningitis & Pneumonia caused by Haemophilus Influenzae type B

milestones: Elimination of maternal and neonatal tetanus in 2015

new_vaccine_introductions.purpose: Reduce mortality and morbidity from rotavirus diarrhea
Achieve measles elimination and rubella control
Reduce infant mortality and morbidity caused by pneumococcal pneumonia
Replaced TT vaccine to address waning immunity against diphtheria in older age groups

immunization_schemes.title: Introduction of Rotavirus Vaccine in UIP
immunization_schemes.description: Oral rotavirus vaccination for children aged 6-32 weeks to prevent severe diarrhea.
how_to_apply: Receive 5 oral drops at UIP session

family_planning_schemes.title: Compensation Package for IUD/Sterilization Acceptors
family_planning_schemes.description: Provides fixed compensation for IUD insertion and sterilization procedures.
family_planning_schemes.eligibility: Women undergoing IUD insertion or sterilization

family_planning_schemes.title: PPIUCD Incentive Scheme
family_planning_schemes.description: Provider incentive for post-partum IUD insertion to promote long-term contraception.
how_to_apply: Avail PPIUCD service at delivery facility

disease_control_schemes.title: RNTCP (Tuberculosis)
disease_control_schemes.description: Free DOTS therapy for tuberculosis patients with persistent cough.

disease_control_schemes.title: NPCDCS: Cancer, Diabetes, CVD & Stroke Control
disease_control_schemes.description: Free screening and subsidized treatment for non-communicable diseases.

financial_support_schemes.title: Free Drugs Service Initiative (FDSI)
financial_support_schemes.description: Government of India provides financial support to ensure essential drugs are available at no cost to patients visiting public healthcare facilities. Contributes to reduction in Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE).
benefits: Free essential drugs at public healthcare facilities

financial_support_schemes.title: Free Diagnostics Service Initiative (FDSI)
financial_support_schemes.description: Government of India provides financial support to ensure essential diagnostics are available at no cost to patients visiting public healthcare facilities. Contributes to reduction in Out-of-Pocket Expenditure (OOPE).
benefits: Free essential diagnostics at public healthcare facilities

antenatal_care.title: Comprehensive Antenatal Care Protocol
antenatal_care.description: Detailed clinical guidelines for antenatal care including registration, visits, examinations, laboratory tests, supplementation, management of common issues, and counseling.

registration.timing: As soon as pregnancy suspected (≤12 weeks)

iron_folic_acid.prophylactic: 1 tablet daily × 100 days (recently shifted from 100mg to 60mg elemental iron)
iron_folic_acid.therapeutic: 2 tablets daily × 100 days if Hb < 11 g/dl

tetanus_toxoid.schedule: 2 doses 1 month apart starting post-1st trimester

supplementation.calcium: 1 tablet (500 mg) twice daily away from IFA

counseling.birth_preparation: Prepare for delivery, discuss birth plan
counseling.nutrition: +300 kcal/day (second & third trimesters), ≥65 g protein/day, adequate fluids ≥2.5 L
counseling.lifestyle: No alcohol/smoking, medications only if prescribed

labour_delivery.title: Labour and Delivery Protocol
labour_delivery.description: Comprehensive guidelines for managing labour and delivery safely, including stages of labor, monitoring, support, delivery procedures, cord management, active third stage management, and essential newborn care.

delivery.episiotomy: Only if indicated (instrumental, fetal distress, previous 3/4° tear)

cord_management.clamping: Clamp at 2 & 5 cm after 2-3 minutes (delayed cord clamping)

active_third_stage.medication: Misoprostol 600 µg PO/SL (alternative: Oxytocin 10 U IM)

postpartum_care.title: Postpartum Care Protocol
postpartum_care.description: Comprehensive care guidelines for mother and baby after delivery, covering observation, postnatal visits, identification of maternal danger signs, and counseling.

neonatal_care_resuscitation.title: Neonatal Care and Resuscitation Protocol
neonatal_care_resuscitation.description: Comprehensive guidelines for newborn care and emergency resuscitation, including routine care, identification of danger signs, management of low birth weight babies, infection management, birth asphyxia resuscitation steps, post-resuscitation care, and practices to avoid.

medications.dose: 2 ml/kg slow IV if metabolic acidosis

stopping_criteria: No breathing for 20-30 minutes despite efforts

state_specific_schemes.description: Enhanced financial assistance to poor pregnant mothers from Rs. 12,000 to Rs. 18,000. Aims for optimal nutrition and wage loss compensation, reducing MMR and IMR. Disbursed in installments, strategically linked to key health behaviors.

installments.condition: Antenatal registration on or before 12 weeks
Completion of third month (First Nutrition Kit)
After completion of all 3rd doses of OPV/Rota/Pentavalent and 2 doses of IPV
After completion of Measles Rubella vaccination (9th-12th month of infant)
